title: ByteLadder: Prompt-Conditioned Progressive Precision for ProMixed KV Caches
hook: ByteLadder adds no action-value network and no counterfactual forward pass at serving time: it reuses ProMixed GQA scores to place independently addressable residual segments under the same exact KV-byte ceiling. The claim is that this strictly leaner runtime axis can outperform uniform-format ProMixed on held-out task categories because precision becomes a byte-by-byte promotion decision rather than a method-wide setting.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: relative to a learned per-action router, ByteLadder adds zero model parameters and zero serving-time teacher passes while retaining a fixed three-profile lookup and one heap traversal. A surprising-empirical hook was also viable, but it was rejected because the direction of the held-out LongBench gain is the falsifiable result, whereas the sharper admission-test fact is the strict reduction in online learned machinery.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved paper tests whether all retained regions in one request must share the same representation and retention rule rather than treating that inherited method-wide uniformity as necessary.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by encoding every historical layer-block as an omittable prefix of fixed-width residual segments and promoting different blocks to P4, P8, or P16 according to task-conditioned value per exact byte, while preserving sensitive blocks with longer prefixes and crushing low-value blocks.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf closes the gap between offline model-level sensitivity and prompt-specific evidence strongly enough to preserve accuracy across task shifts while keeping selection overhead inside the serving deadline.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by retrieving three offline task-category promotion profiles from a canonical ProMixed prompt fingerprint and composing their layer-by-rung gains at inference, with entire task categories held out and no per-task parameter update.

core_mechanism: ByteLadder is a sequential pipeline whose central object is a request-specific precision-promotion heap over the same 16-token historical blocks already scored by ProMixed; the mandatory recent window and attention sinks remain FP16, and their allocator-reported bytes are subtracted from the request KV ceiling before routing. For each layer l and block b, let X_lb be the FP16 key/value tensor emitted by prefill; fixed groups of 64 scalars are successively quantized as q1=Q4(X_lb), q2=Q4(X_lb-q1), and q3=Q8(X_lb-q1-q2), giving modes omit, P4={q1}, P8={q1,q2}, and P16={q1,q2,q3}. Qq uses a stored per-group scale max(abs(residual))/(2^(q-1)-1), round-to-nearest signed integers, and no clipping, so each reconstruction is a prefix sum and the omitted suffix is an exact residual decomposition; each quantization stage also has the auditable infinity-norm rounding bound scale/2, without claiming a downstream accuracy certificate. Offline, for each LongBench task category j, every model layer l, and promotion rung u in {omit→P4,P4→P8,P8→P16}, the reference bank stores g_jlu, the mean reduction in full-cache teacher-forced suffix KL produced by that promotion on calibration prompts, plus a centroid mu_j of a canonical prompt fingerprint. The fingerprint z is computed only from model-internal ProMixed readouts: for every layer, normalized GQA block-score entropy, top-k pairwise Jaccard agreement, and the kept-versus-next boundary margin are averaged within four deterministic depth strata floor(4l/L), where L is read from the model configuration, producing twelve values. At runtime the top R=3 centroids under diagonal-whitened squared distance d_j=(z-mu_j)^T diag(var+1e-4)^(-1)(z-mu_j) receive weights w_j=softmax(-d_j/tau), with tau chosen once on validation task categories, and the conditioned promotion gain is ghat_lu(z)=sum_j w_j g_jlu. ProMixed already supplies a dimensionless block utility s_lb from its scale-normalized max/mean/vote fusion; the current frontier promotion for each block receives value v_lbu=s_lb*ghat_lu and priority v_lbu divided by its exact incremental bytes, including dense code bits, scales, block headers, and alignment. A max-heap starts with omit→P4 for every historical block, accepts the highest-priority item only when its predecessor is present and its bytes fit, then exposes that block's next rung; therefore B_used equals the mandatory bytes plus the accepted segment bytes and is always at most the exact ceiling B, although unused slack smaller than the next segment is allowed. The accepted prefixes are materialized once after prefill and decoded by fused residual-add attention kernels; TTFT, throughput, and conversion overhead are measured end to end, but no sum of kernel quantiles is presented as a hard wall-clock guarantee.
core_mechanism_reasoning: The two gaps share a sequential dependency rather than one predictor: task-category profiles first condition layer-level promotion gains, and ProMixed prompt scores then place the resulting residual segments under the byte ceiling. An action-specific counterfactual predictor plus a two-resource program was rejected because it would need an unsupported hard latency cost model; a fixed Oaken-style threshold was rejected because it regresses to method-wide calibration, while fixed positional windows, attention-mass-only eviction, head sharing, paging, and offloading are occupied lineage nodes that do not supply prompt-conditioned precision promotion.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Add a progressive KV codec beside the existing Qwen2.5-7B Re-Prefill path; input is each FP16 16-token layer-block X_lb, and output is three fixed-width residual segments plus exact byte metadata.
2. Build the offline reference bank from LongBench training categories by running full-cache and single-rung promotion replays over teacher-forced suffixes; inputs are calibration prompts and frozen Qwen2.5-7B, and outputs are g_jlu tables, fingerprint centroids mu_j, and diagonal variances.
3. Split LongBench by entire task category, tune only tau and the 1e-4 variance floor on validation categories, and serialize the bank; input is reference profiles, and output is one immutable runtime table with no task-specific weights.
4. During prefill, retain the existing ProMixed GQA block-score rows for every layer and compute entropy, agreement, and boundary margin; input is the existing selector readout, and output is the twelve-dimensional request fingerprint z and block utilities s_lb.
5. Retrieve the three nearest profile centroids, compute w_j and ghat_lu, and emit one initial omit→P4 promotion item for each historical block; input is z, s_lb, and the bank, and output is a max-heap keyed by conditioned gain per exact incremental byte.
6. Subtract the allocator-reported bytes of mandatory FP16 recent-window and sink entries from B, pop the heap until no frontier item fits, and expose a block's next rung only after accepting its predecessor; input is the heap and byte ceiling, and output is one feasible mode per block plus B_used≤B.
7. Materialize only accepted residual segments into aligned cache pages and record mode offsets; input is the mode map and prefill X_lb tensors, and output is the physical mixed-format KV cache whose measured allocation matches B_used.
8. Extend the attention load path with fused P4, P8, and P16 residual reconstruction before the existing dot product; input is the mixed-format pages and decode queries, and output is the ordinary attention result that changes generated answers through the unchanged remaining Qwen layers.
9. Log actual KV bytes, conversion time, TTFT, decode throughput, and downstream predictions for every request; input is serving traces and benchmark labels, and output is a paired comparison against uniform-format ProMixed, DynamicKV-style layer budgets, Oaken-style fixed calibration, and global-profile ByteLadder.
10. Run the profile-permutation negative control and oracle-category positive control without changing bytes or ProMixed scores; input is the same prompts with altered ghat_lu, and output is the causal test of whether profile conditioning drives held-out accuracy.
falsification_prediction: On Qwen2.5-7B, hold out complete LongBench task categories from the reference bank and evaluate those categories plus Needle-in-a-Haystack at 5%, 10%, and 25% allocator-measured historical-KV byte ceilings against uniform-format ProMixed and global-profile ByteLadder, while reporting actual TTFT rather than enforcing a wall-clock claim. If ByteLadder works, held-out LongBench score and NIAH exact-match increase at the same or lower measured KV bytes, with the largest gain at 5% and 10%; P95 TTFT is a separately reported deployment outcome and may rise or fall. The single load-bearing variable is the prompt-conditioned promotion-gain table ghat_lu(z). As a negative control, randomly permute the association between profile centroids and their g_jlu tables while leaving ProMixed scores, residual codec, and exact byte packing unchanged; the downstream LongBench and NIAH gains should return toward the global-profile ByteLadder or uniform-format ProMixed baseline, while an oracle task-category profile should recover most of the gain as a positive control.
compute_budget: Approximately 42 GPU-days on 80GB-class A100/H100 GPUs (about 24 for offline promotion profiling and 18 for held-out LongBench/NIAH serving, baselines, controls, and two implementation iterations) + $0 paid API inference; comfortable within the stated ~150 GPU-day and ~$10k envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: DynamicKV periodically renormalizes layer-specific retained-token counts from prefill attention under a token budget, whereas ByteLadder allocates independently addressable precision residuals and omission at 16-token block granularity under allocator-measured bytes, conditioned by profiles learned with entire task categories held out.

Oaken calibrates data-agnostic outlier thresholds offline and selects quantization scales online inside a fixed low-bit hardware format, whereas ByteLadder retrieves a request-conditioned layer-by-rung promotion table and chooses how many residual segments each block receives.

Ecco fixes a 64-byte compressed block and power-of-two compression ratio with shared k-means and Huffman structures, whereas ByteLadder exposes fixed-width residual segments as separately allocatable units so a request can mix omit, P4, P8, and P16 modes without exceeding its exact byte ceiling.

ChunkKV changes the pruning unit to semantic chunks and reuses selected indices across layers but still makes retain-or-drop decisions under one representation, while ByteLadder keeps the existing ProMixed block unit and promotes block representations to different precision prefixes.

what_step_was_missed: Oaken would have needed to replace its fixed online-offline low-bit format with independently addressable successive-residual segments and bind their per-request promotion order to a held-out-task profile retrieved from prompt-specific GQA evidence.
